newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends up on Tokyo shortcovering.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends up on Tokyo shortcovering.

text.p: Hong Kong spot gold ended up on Thursday from New York's previous close after a shortcovering rally overcame gold's dip from earlier sales, traders said.
Bullion ended at US$348.20/70 an ounce against New York's US$347.80/348.30 close on Wednesday.
Bullion dealers said traders in Japan sold gold in the morning, but the dollar edged down slightly later in the day and led to shortcovering in gold markets.
The early afternoon gold price hike attracted European selling, which pushed gold back to a closing price away from the day's high at $348.60/349.10 per ounce.
"It's been quite volatile," said one bullion dealer.
Physical gold was said quiet as buyers waited for more stability, dealers said.
Local gold ended HK$7 higher at HK$3,226 a tael.
The carry over charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society dropped to nil from its previous fix at +2.00
